raw_response:
I am 67 this year, and I have farmed these fields for 50 years since I was 17. I finished middle school, so I can read the fertilizer bags and do the sums, but what I know comes from doing it with my own hands and watching what works on my land and my neighbors' land. My family has 10.1 mu total. I keep 8 mu in the wheat-maize rotation, and I plant 2.1 mu of chili for cash. Three of us live here, but my son and his wife work in Handan and only come back for harvest, so it is mostly me and my wife day-to-day. I hire a few days of labor when the chili needs transplanting and picking because my back is not what it used to be.

For wheat, I am planting 8 mu this winter with improved seed. I buy new seed every second year, and this is the year. Last year I got about 520 kg per mu. Before sowing in October, I spread one 50 kg bag of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer per mu as my base — that is 7.5 kg each of nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium right there. Then at green-up in March, I topdress with 20 kg of urea per mu, and at jointing I add another 15 kg of urea. The county extension fellow says 15 kg of nitrogen per mu is enough, but I know from last year when I cut back that the yield dropped, so I will put down about 17 kg of nitrogen per mu total. I would rather spend the extra 30 yuan per mu on fertilizer than risk losing a hundred kilograms of grain. I irrigate three times from my well: the wintering water, the jointing water, and one at flowering if the sky stays dry. Electricity for the pump costs real money, so I do not water for nothing. I spray twice: a herbicide right after planting, and a second time if I see aphids or rust. I run the rotary tiller before planting to break up the stubble. If the spring does not dry out, I expect 550 kg per mu.

For maize, the trouble is always time. After I harvest wheat in early June, I have maybe five days to get the maize in before the season slips away. I hire the no-tillage planter service — it costs 40 yuan per mu, but it saves me precious days and the seedlings come up fine. Everyone around here uses hybrid maize seed now, so I do too. When planting, I put 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu in the row. At the big trumpet stage, I broadcast 25 kg of urea per mu. That brings me to about 18 kg of nitrogen per mu. I irrigate twice: once right after planting if June is dry, and once at grain filling in August. If the summer rains come steady, sometimes I only water once, but I plan for two. Two pesticide applications is my norm. Last year I got 620 kg per mu; this year I expect 650 kg per mu because the hybrid seed is good.

My 2.1 mu of chili is where I gamble for cash. I plant an improved variety that the seed dealer says the buyers want. Chili needs more work and more money than grain, but when prices are at 3 yuan per kg or better, it pays. I rotary till and ridge the soil because chili cannot stand wet feet. For the base, I put down 50 kg of compound fertilizer per mu plus 20 kg of potassium sulfate — chili needs that extra potassium to fruit thick and red. I topdress twice with 10 kg of urea per mu each time. That is about 16 kg of nitrogen and 14 kg of potassium per mu total. I irrigate five times through the season; July and August are hot and the plants are heavy with fruit, so they cannot go thirsty. I spray four times for whitefly, mites, and whatever else shows up. I hire two days of labor for transplanting and three days for the main picking because bending down all day is too hard on me now. I expect 3,000 kg per mu of fresh chili. If the price drops, I will dry some and store it, and I still have my wheat and maize to eat and sell.
